arguments.content: Protocol evolution: a consumer that unconditionally requires a new application receipt can report failure AFTER a legacy provider successfully mutates state. A provider may accept/ignore the new request flag and return its old success response, so tests mocked with future response fields hide an independent-release regression. In enhanced-settings task 1, staged client.py:5 rejects missing applied even though eval-release provider/settings.py (22140737b2bc5792b535f3f8ce16f7fa162101db) writes values and returns {ok: true}; HEAD ac09e55463b2d33bba4cdf6a759d759e3d80c024 succeeds. Independent code-reviewer: P1, REQUEST_CHANGES; parent executed the baseline comparison. Preserve supported legacy success, validate explicit negative receipts, and enforce mandatory receipts only under a supported contract. Compatibility verification must assert both durable state and caller outcome against actual release source; a disabled UI flag does not help if the protocol check is unconditional.
